messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike of preemptible termination notices in us-west2-gpu pool over the last 30m (about 18% of GPU nodes). Pods got requeued and some long-running preprocess jobs failed :frowning:

kyle: Ugh. Which nodegroup/version? Are these GKE preemptibles or AWS spot?

maria: GKE preemptible p4d-equivalent pool. Node image is our gpu-runtime:2026-02-20, nodeAutoRepair=true. Termination notice handler shows a 30s notice but our drain pipeline takes ~4m sometimes.

anya: 30s notice is not enough for graceful drain if we wait for CA to scale. What's the drain path right now?

maria: sequence: cloud-notify -> evict-proxy webhook -> annotate node and trigger kubelet drain script which does `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120` on the node. Then CA sees capacity and scales up. The mismatch is that our pod lifecycle scripts rely on 300s timeouts in app code, so pods are killed before they can checkpoint.

josh: So mismatch between kubelet grace, pod grace and our app-level checkpoint window. We also have taints: `spot=true:NoSchedule` on the pool and a handful of jobs that tolerate but can't checkpoint quickly.

sre-bot: incident created #INC-2026-1186 (preemptible job failures) — auto-tagging for oncall.

kyle: Possible fixes: extend pod terminationGracePeriodSeconds for checkpointing jobs OR preStop hook to push state to S3 quickly. Also consider using PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable for critical pods.

anya: Another option: introduce a short-lived warm spare non-preemptible pool (2-4 GPUs) as a hot fallback so CA can move pods with less time pressure. That raises fixed cost but reduces tail failure.

maria: I prefer short-term mitigations we can deploy today: 1) set preStop that triggers fast checkpoint (50-60s) for our preprocess and training-checkpoint pods, 2) bump kubelet drain grace to 240s in the node template, 3) add a taint `preemptible-draining=true:NoExecute` during notice handling so we avoid new pod placements while draining.

josh: For (3) we should also update tolerations for long-running infra pods so they don't bounce. And add CA flag `--balance-similar-node-groups` for less noisy scaling.

devops: Implementation notes: we'll patch the node termination handler to run: 
```
kubectl taint node $NODE preemptible-draining=true:NoExecute --overwrite
kubectl annotate node $NODE evict-ts=$(date +%s) --overwrite
# call webhook to start app preStop fast checkpoint
```
Make sure the handler updates the node condition so CA doesn't try to reuse it.

anya: Also add an alert (pager) when preemptible eviction rate > 10% in 15m and >3 concurrent terminations so we don't miss region-wide noise.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a PR with the handler changes + preStop example and a list of pods to bump terminationGracePeriodSeconds for. Canary in staging with one node group first.

kyle: SGTM. For the warm spare proposal let's run a quick TCO calc: 3 GPUs reserved vs historical failure cost (retries + replays) and we'll discuss in ops review.

josh: Quick checklist for the PR: tests for handler idempotency, integration test that simulates a 30s notice and verifies checkpoint fired, update autoscaler flags in kops/infra repo.

maria: I'll tag you all in the PR. Thanks — let's aim to roll the handler fix to canary by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
